column2: Culture-first: a love letter to the world's most-eaten food. Not character-first cute.
Plush / throw pillow, Squishmallow-adjacent. Kids are the ones who love it. Under $100.
Stickers stay in the line as the cheap way in. Score people on the flagship; the 'Would buy' column records which they'd actually buy.
All three: kawaii/stationery collectors, food-culture people, diaspora 'rice is home'.
Buyer and user are different people. An adult pays, a child hugs it. A high score with no child in their life is a gift-buyer, not a household customer.
Lots of 'Stickers only' is a real answer, not a failure. It means the brand works and $100 is the wrong first product.
Score people as they are, not as you hope. A sheet of generous 4s tells you nothing you didn't already believe.
